failure_mode: cavitation erosion of propeller blade surfaces
failure: Documented marine engineering problem: propeller blade sections operating at high loading develop local vapor cavities that collapse near the blade surface, eroding the bronze and pitting the leading edge and outer blade sections; erosion costs fuel (roughened surface, degraded efficiency), forces early drydocking and propeller repair or replacement, and can progress to blade thinning and vibration. Known mitigations exist (polishing, coatings, air injection, design revision of skew/camber) — a candidate that merely restates these is not differentiated. Qualitative engineering-literature context; no fabricated statistics (retrieval must custody the evidence).
constraint: Retrofit must apply to existing propellers without re-casting or re-designing the blade geometry, must survive cavitation collapse loading and seawater corrosion for at least one 5-year drydock interval, must not reduce propulsive efficiency by more than 0.5%, and must be applicable during routine drydocking.

sources.problem_basis: engineering-literature qualitative context; no fabricated statistics
